title: Dili International Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Edition Was Like
meta_description: Dili International Marathon 2026 review: Chinese wins in the marathon, a Timorese half-marathon winner, adaptive races, and what runners said on 8 August.
dek: Timor-Leste's flagship race was run through Dili on Saturday 8 August 2026, with international elites, an Australian Defence Force team and an adaptive 10 km. Here is what it was like, from the report on it.
verdict: The Dili International Marathon is Timor-Leste's flagship athletic event, backed by the Presidential Palace [1]. The 2026 edition, on Saturday 8 August, was won by China's Bangliu Zhang and Jiali Wang in the marathon, while Timorese runner Felisberto de Deus won the half marathon ahead of an Australian [1]. The race included an adaptive 10 km for athletes with disabilities [1], and the runners who spoke afterwards praised the scenery and the day [1]. If you want a marathon somewhere few runners have raced, with a genuine national-occasion feel, it is a rewarding choice.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: The race was run on Saturday 8 August 2026 in Dili [1]. It brings together thousands of domestic and international athletes to promote peace, fitness and sports tourism, alongside an expo that showcases local industry and community health [1].

There were races over the full marathon, the half marathon and a 10 km, including an adaptive 10 km for athletes with disabilities [1]. An Australian Defence Force team was among the visiting runners [1].

sections.heading: What the Winners Said
paragraphs: Bangliu Zhang won the men's marathon on debut, and said his main goal had been a good position and a good result [1]. Jiali Wang, the women's winner, said she enjoyed the scenery and seeing different parts of Timor-Leste, and that she ran with several Timorese athletes early on, whom she found very strong, before pulling away as the pace rose [1].

In the half marathon, Felisberto de Deus beat Australia's Kieren, who said the two ran together until the Timorese runner opened a gap at about 8 km, and that the day and the experience were excellent [1]. Teófilo Freitas won the adaptive 10 km and thanked the Presidential Palace for including athletes with disabilities in the race [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you want a marathon with a sense of occasion in a country few runners visit, yes. The winners' accounts describe a scenic course and a competitive local field.
Plan the trip, not just the race. Dili is a small capital with limited flights, so book travel early and leave room either side of race day.
This review is compiled from a published report on the 2026 edition, including runners' comments to reporters. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: Who won the Dili International Marathon in 2026?
faqs.answer: China's Bangliu Zhang won the men's marathon and Jiali Wang the women's on Saturday 8 August 2026. Timorese runner Felisberto de Deus won the men's half marathon ahead of an Australian runner, and Teófilo Freitas won the adaptive 10 km.

faqs.question: Does the Dili International Marathon include athletes with disabilities?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 2026 race included an adaptive 10 km event for athletes with disabilities. Its winner, Teófilo Freitas, thanked the Presidential Palace for including disabled athletes in the country's flagship race.

faqs.question: What is the Dili International Marathon like to run?
faqs.answer: Scenic and competitive, by the runners' own accounts. The 2026 women's winner said she enjoyed the scenery and found the Timorese runners she started with very strong, and the runner-up in the half marathon called the day and the experience excellent.
